science.title: Brain possesses greater self-repair capacity than previously assumed
science.description: The brain evidently can regenerate itself better than previously assumed after injuries or certain autoimmune diseases. Using a mouse model, researchers at the University of Zurich have demonstrated that special supporting and nourishing cells repopulate damaged areas of the brain by initially sending only newly formed cell nuclei there.

science.title: 240-million-year-old reptile fossil reveals a lost chapter before dinosaurs and crocodiles
science.description: A 240-million-year-old reptile discovered in Brazil is revealing what evolution looked like just before the rise of dinosaurs and crocodiles. The small predator had unusually positioned legs that may have allowed it to move more efficiently than many earlier reptiles. Its close relatives were previously known mostly from other continents, suggesting these ancient animals spread much farther across the Triassic world than scientists realized.

science.title: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
science.description: The rise of the potato in the Andes appears to have left a lasting mark on human DNA. Indigenous Peruvians carry exceptionally high numbers of a starch-digestion gene, likely because people with more copies gained an evolutionary advantage once potatoes became a staple food. The change began thousands of years before European contact, providing unusually strong evidence that diet can shape human evolution.

science.description: Since it became operational in 2022, the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has released some truly breathtaking views of the cosmos. These images highlight how advancements since the days of the venerable Hubble Space Telescope are now providing the deepest and clearest views of the cosmos to date. The work is published on the arXiv preprint server.

science.title: Revealed: mitochondria act as sensors for essential iron molecule
science.description: Heme, a bioactive form of iron, has numerous essential functions in the cell. As a key component of hemoglobin, it enables oxygen transport in the blood. ai.title: Innefu Labs: India's Palantir Building the Sovereign AI Backbone for National Security
ai.description: New Delhi [India], August 10: As nations increasingly treat data sovereignty as a matter of national security, one name comes up consistently among those tracking the space in India: Innefu Labs, the artificial intelligence company in the space of national security that industry watchers regularly describe as India's Palantir. Over more than a decade, its platforms have become embedded across the country's defence, intelligence, law enforcement, and revenue intelligence establishments, not as a single system, but as the sovereign technological backbone of India's most sensitive institutions.
